items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Then it was supposed to be like Artie Shaw you know.

ctx.x: That’s a great story. I had something about you playing with a fellow named Jerry Wald?

Jerry Wald. He thought he was — after a while, when I first got with him he was imitating Hal Kemp, the clarinet would be in megaphones with their hands through and it’s a lot to get out of that kind of music [scats], but then Artie Shaw retired and Jerry got the big idea, so nearly overnight he got all of his arrangements, and the whole band changed. Then it was supposed to be like Artie Shaw you know. Yeah I worked with him in the Spanish Gardens in New York, did a broadcast, you know we were on, I guess every…
What age were you when you moved away, moved out of your family house?
